spec.name: Reversal v21
spec.notes: Mean reversion of recent returns across names.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.2, annual return 8%, maximum drawdown 2%.

verdict.opinion: The strategy relies on a very small sample size of only four distinct specifications. With such a limited search space, the reported Sharpe ratio of 2.2 is highly susceptible to selection bias and lucky period performance. The lack of rigorous out-of-sample testing or cross-validation makes it impossible to determine if the alpha is robust or merely a result of overfitting to the specific historical window. Given the high sensitivity of mean-reversion strategies to transaction costs and market regime shifts, deploying real capital is premature. I recommend paper trading to verify if the signal persists under live market conditions before committing any funds.
